question: Why does volume control not work on Huya / Douyin live streams?

targetSelection.huya_live: activeMedia media:1 (video), selection=2 in 76 of 82 live snapshots; selection=1 in 6
targetSelection.douyin_live: activeMedia media:2 (video), selection=5 in 10 of 11 live snapshots
targetSelection.conclusion: Selection is stable and correct. No thrashing, no wrong preview/video selected.

volumeWrites.state: every value: phase=applied, strategy=dom-native, desired===actual, lastError=null
volumeWrites.observations: controlled:false snapshots (post-write observations) also report actual===desired, so the player does NOT restore element.volume afterwards
volumeWrites.conclusion: element.volume is physically written and read back correctly and stays there. The extension's write path is NOT broken.

only_errors: capability-unavailable / 'No active media target' during tab navigation (all four fields at once)
capability-unavailable / 'A live stream has no playback rate to change' for speed=2 (by design, media-live.ts)

audioSession.capture: 19 snapshots desiredMode=actualMode=capture, volume=105/115/145, volumeBase=100, strategy=capture, phase=applied
audioSession.note: capture mode starts and ACKs successfully on the Huya live document (589FCD395BB358EA30F04DF8097C5832), proving the extension's WebAudio processor can own that tab's audio path.

rootCause: On live pages the audible signal is not emitted through HTMLMediaElement.volume: players route live audio through their own WebAudio/player pipeline (video element carries no usable audio track). Writing element.volume succeeds and reads back correctly but does not change what the viewer hears. This is exactly the 'changes the displayed volume without changing sound' symptom recorded in docs/research/2026-09-23-spectra-douyin-route-isolation.md, whose final line already states live sound control was never verified on a real device.
whyPreviousFixesDidNotWork: Every prior attempt changed control logic (discovery cache, native reconciliation, strict/loose readback, audio focus, unmute guard). This evidence shows control logic reports success with the correct target, so those changes could not affect the audible path.
architecturalConstraint: CONTROL_VALUE_LIMITS.boost = {min:1,max:8}; AudioProcessorConfig.boostGain validates against the same 'boost' limit and its contract comment states 'Processor gain is Boost only. Page volume and media mute remain owned by the standard DOM/allowlisted official-player writers'. Routing 0-100 live volume through the processor therefore requires a contract + state-machine change (allow attenuation), not a local fix in the executor.
openQuestion: Which object actually emits the live audio (page GainNode, MediaStreamAudioSourceNode, or a proprietary player pipeline)? Required before choosing between (a) processor attenuation via tabCapture, (b) a declared volume adapter for the player's real audio API, or (c) hooking the page's output GainNode.
